# Linearized read / ordinary full-save fixtures

Project-authored two-page geometry (blue and red rectangles, 200 × 200 pt),
with explicit empty page Resources dictionaries. No text, embedded fonts,
external documents or third-party creative assets. Content uses the repository
AGPL-3.0-only license; producer binaries and private keys are not redistributed.

The base fixtures were generated using qpdf 11.2.0 from a hand-authored PDF 1.7:

- `qpdf --linearize source.pdf two-pages.pdf`
- `qpdf --linearize --object-streams=generate source.pdf two-pages-objects.pdf`

Both pass `qpdf --check` as linearized PDFs. The second also exercises xref/object
streams. Native and browser tests consume committed bytes, requiring no producer.
Local Git attributes keep PDF bytes binary, preserving xref padding and signed ranges.

The [follow-up generator](../../../../scripts/prepare_linearized_followup.py)
accepts a new output directory and requires existing qpdf/OpenSSL:

- `two-pages-overflow.pdf`: the original decoded 64-byte hint payload split at
  byte 20. Concatenating decoded primary and overflow data recovers the original
  bytes, including the shared-object hint table at offset 38. Existing page-object
  offsets stay fixed. Both hint identities are in the first xref table; the
  overflow object follows the page objects. qpdf confirms valid linearization.
- `two-pages-r6.pdf`: qpdf AES-256/R6 linearized output. Synthetic passwords:
  `synthetic-user` / `synthetic-owner`. Both have all document permissions.
- `two-pages-signed.pdf`: the complete ordinary base fixture prefix followed by
  a real detached SHA-256/RSA CMS approval revision with a hidden signature widget.
  The original `/Linearized` remains in that signed prefix; the appended file is
  correctly reported as **not currently linearized**. OpenSSL independently verifies
  the signature with `-noverify` (no certificate trust claim). This tests writing
  guards for a formerly linearized source, not acceptance of linearized signature
  history. The one-day synthetic certificate is embedded; its key is only generated
  in the ignored output directory and is unnecessary for verification or tests.

The follow-up manifest records producer versions, binary hashes and qpdf checks.
Random R6 keys/IVs and a new ephemeral signer change regenerated bytes. No test
requires deterministic cryptographic output, certificate trust or network access.
